2 	title: cacheComponents
3 	description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
4 	related:
5 	  links:
6 	    - app/getting-started/caching
7 	    - app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components
8 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache
9 	    - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote
10	---
11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file:
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	}
24	
25	export default nextConfig
26	```
27	
28	> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime. Migrate any routes that set the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'` export, and note that other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
29	
30	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
31	
32	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
33	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
34	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
35	
36	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
37	
38	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
39	
40	Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
41	
42	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
43	
44	## Navigation with Activity
45	
46	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
47	
48	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
49	
50	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
51	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
52	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
53	
54	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
55	
56	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
57	
58	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/gu

13 	
14 	> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
15 	
16 	Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.
17 	
18 	## Enabling Cache Components
19 	
20 	You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:
21 	
22 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
23 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
24 	
25 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
26 	  cacheComponents: true,
27 	}
28 	
29 	export default nextConfig
30 	```
31 	
32 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
33 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
34 	const nextConfig = {
35 	  cacheComponents: true,
36 	}
37 	
38 	module.exports = nextConfig
39 	```
40 	
41 	> **Good to know:** When Cache Components is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerendering model as pages. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details.
42 	
43 	## Usage
44 	
45 	The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels:
46 	
47 	- **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`)
48 	- **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`)
49 	
50 	A cache directive gives a result a lifetime, which Next.js uses for time-based revalidation and rendering optimizations. For on-demand revalidation after a mutation, see [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). See [Prerendering](#prerendering) for how cached results become part of the static shell and may be included in a [prefetch](#prefetching).
51 	
52 	> **Good to know:** We recommend pairing every cache directive with a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). Without one, the implicit `default` profile applies.
53 	
54 	Arguments and any values captured from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries. See [cache output](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-output) for what an entry holds, and [serialization requirements and constraints](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#constraints) for details on what can be cached and how arguments work.
55 	
56 	### Data-level caching
57 	
58 	To cache an asynchronous function that fetches data, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the function body:
59 	
60 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
61 	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
62 	
63 	export async function getUsers() {
64 	  'use cache'
65 	  cacheLife('hours')
66 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM users')
67 	}
68 	```
69 	
70 	Data-level caching is useful when the same data is used across multiple components, or when you want to cache the data independently from the UI.
71 	
72 	### UI-level caching

1  	---
2  	title: Incremental Static Regeneration with Cache Components
3  	description: Learn how to prerender a subset of dynamic routes, serve App Shells for the rest, and upgrade them after the first visit.
4  	nav_title: ISR with Cache Components
5  	related:
6  	  links:
7  	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
8  	    - app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params
9  	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading
10 	    - app/getting-started/caching
11 	---
12 	
13 	[Incremental Static Regeneration (ISR)](/docs/app/glossary#incremental-static-regeneration-isr) with [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) gives every route an instant first visit, even for URLs that weren't included in the build.
14 	
15 	During build, Partial Prerendering splits each render into two parts:
16 	
17 	- The **App Shell**: the generic, reusable part of the page that doesn't depend on URL data
18 	- The rest of the statically renderable content: the param-specific prerenders for the URLs you list in [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params)
19 	
20 	For a visit to a URL whose params were included in `generateStaticParams`, Next.js serves the fully prerendered page from the cache. For a visit to a URL whose params weren't, Next.js serves the App Shell instantly, then upgrades it in the background with the now-known params. Subsequent visits to that URL get the upgraded result from the cache, skipping the App Shell entirely.
21 	
22 	If you have used [ISR](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration) or [`fallback: true`](https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths#fallback-true) in the Pages Router, this is the Cache Components equivalent.
23 	
24 	Enable both [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching).
25 	
26 	Cache Components prerenders a static shell that can include fallback UI. For paths not returned by `generateStaticParams`, Next.js can render the path on demand and store the completed result in the ISR cache.
27 	
28 	Partial Prefetching determines whether the fallback is served before the URL-specific render completes:
29 	
30 	- **With Partial Prefetching:** You can await `params` inside `<Suspense>`. Next.js can immediately serve the fallback for an unlisted path, render the URL-specific content, and store the completed result in the ISR cache.
31 	- **Without Partial Prefetching:** The first request for an unlisted path must wait for the URL-specific render to complete. Await `params` outside any `<Suspense>` boundary, including one created by [`loading.tsx`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading), so Next.js creates an ISR entry for that URL.
32 	
33 	> **Good to know:** Without Partial Prefetching, awaiting `params` inside `<Suspense>` causes Next.js to keep serving the shared fallback instead of creating a URL-specific ISR entry. Data fetched by the route can still be cached independently.
34 	
35 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4-5}
36 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
37 	
38 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
39 	  cacheComponents: true,
40 	  partialPrefetching: true,
41 	}
42 	
43 	export default nextConfig
44 	```
45 	
46 	## Example
47 	
48 	We'll build a product catalog with category layouts and product detail pages using the [Recipe API](https://next-recipe-api.vercel.dev/). You can find the resources used in this example here:
49 	
50 	- [Demo](https://partial-fallbacks.labs.vercel.dev/)
51 	- [Code](https://github.com/vercel-labs/partial-fallbacks)
52 	
53 	### Prepare your routes
54 	
55 	Use [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params) to define which param

2  	title: Ensuring instant navigations
3  	description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations.

5  	related:

8  	  links:

14 	---
15 	
16 	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
17 	
18 	## What "instant" means
19 	
20 	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
21 	
22 	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
23 	
24 	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
25 	
26 	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
27 	
28 	<details>
29 	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
30 	
31 	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
32 	
33 	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
34 	
35 	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
36 	
37 	</details>
38 	
39 	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.
40 	
41 	## Quick start
42 	
43 	Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear:
44 	
45 	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
46 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
47 	
48 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
49 	  cacheComponents: true,
50 	  partialPrefetching: true,
51 	}
52 	
53 	export default nextConfig
54 	```
55 	
56 	To help you automate this process with an agent, there's a Skill for each part, [next-cache-components-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) and [next-partial-prefetching-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption).

15 	
16 	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
17 	
18 	## What "instant" means
19 	
20 	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
21 	
22 	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
23 	
24 	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
25 	
26 	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
27 	
28 	<details>
29 	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
30 	
31 	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
32 	
33 	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
34 	
35 	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
36 	
37 	</details>
38 	
39 	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.
40 	
41 	## Quick start
42 	
43 	Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear:
44 	
45 	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
46 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
47 	
48 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
49 	  cacheComponents: true,
50 	  partialPrefetching: true,
51 	}
52 	
53 	export default nextConfig
54 	```
55

Calling it at the top level of a file will throw an error. 45 46 > **Good to know**: 47 > 48 > - We recommend setting a `cacheLife` in every `use cache` scope so its behavior is clear at the call site. Avoid abstracting it into shared utilities so the cache behavior remains explicit and easy to reason about. 50 > - If you call `cacheLife`, ensure only one call executes per function invocation. You can call it in different control flow branches, but only one should run per request. See the [conditional cache lifetimes](#conditional-cache-lifetimes) example. 51 52 ### Using preset profiles 53 54 Next.js provides preset cache profiles that cover common caching needs. Each profile balances three factors: 55 56 - How long users see cached content without checking for updates (client-side) 57 - How often fresh content is generated on the server 58 - When old content expires completely 59 60 Choose a profile based on how frequently your content changes: 61 62 - **`seconds`** - Real-time data (stock prices, live scores) 63 - **`minutes`** - Frequently updated (social feeds, news) 64 - **`hours`** - Multiple daily updates (product inventory, weather) 65 - **`days`** - Daily updates (blog posts, articles) 66 - **`weeks`** - Weekly updates (podcasts, newsletters) 67 - **`max`** - Rarely changes (legal pages, archived content) 68 69 Import `cacheLife` and pass a profile name: 70 71 ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" highlight={1,5} 72 'use cache' 73 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 74 75 export default async function BlogPage() { 76 cacheLife('days') // Blog content updated daily 77 78 const posts = await getBlogPosts() 79 return

You can prerender loading indicators such as skeletons and spinners, or a small but meaningful part of future screens such as a cover photo, title, etc. This helps users understand the app is responding and provides a better user experience. 51 52 Create a loading state by adding a `loading.js` file inside a folder. 53 54 61 62 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/loading.tsx" switcher 63 export default function Loading() { 64 // You can add any UI inside Loading, including a Skeleton. 65 return 66 } 67 ``` 68 69 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/loading.js" switcher 70 export default function Loading() { 71 // You can add any UI inside Loading, including a Skeleton. 72 return 73 } 74 ``` 75 76 In the same folder, `loading.js` will be nested inside `layout.js`. It will automatically wrap the `page.js` file and any children below in a `` boundary. 77 78

events.content:
Cache Components is on, and the production build completed without route opt-outs.

- The product details are cached with `use cache`, keyed by the slug and the currency, so `/products/lamp?currency=EUR` stays `EUR 110.40` and `/products/vase` stays `USD 80.00`.
- The shop frame (nav, collection label, and related heading) is in the static shell with loading fallbacks.
- Related products stay uncached in their own Suspense boundary and stream after the details.

`npm run build` passed with exit code 0. `/` is static, and `/products/[slug]` is a partial prerender.
